query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Reducing the nozzle‐to‐substrate distance on the HVAF-i7 torch to a value in the 300–350 mm range will increase particle velocity during deposition and thereby overcome the current thickness limitation for FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy bond coats.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy powders with a 15–45 μm feedstock prepared for HVAF deposition.
generation.intervention: Adjust the HVAF-i7 torch parameters by reducing the spray distance to approximately 300–350 mm.
generation.conditions: Deposition using the HVAF-i7 process on substrates suitable for small internal diameters (down to ~120 mm) and designed for high-temperature thermal-barrier service, under otherwise standard operating conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: Increased particle kinetic energy leading to enhanced splat formation and improved inter-particle bonding.
generation.mechanism: Reducing the spray distance increases the particle velocity, which in turn raises the kinetic energy of the particles upon impact with the substrate. This results in a denser build-up and improved adhesion, allowing a thicker bond coat to form with minimal in-flight oxidation.
generation.predicted_outcome: A bond coat with a significantly increased thickness compared to the current baseline (using default HVAF-i7 parameters) while maintaining acceptable adhesion and low as-sprayed oxidation levels.
generation.baseline: Coatings produced with 15–45 μm feedstock using the current HVAF-i7 settings that yield acceptable quality but insufficient thickness.
generation.boundary: This approach should be effective as long as the spray distance is kept within the 300–350 mm range and particle overheating or excessive oxidation due to too high velocity is avoided. Its performance may be compromised if other parameters (e.g., gas flow or feed rate) deviate substantially from the standard settings.
generation.uncertainty: While increased particle velocity is expected to improve deposition efficiency, the precise impact on oxidation kinetics and coating microstructure under varied thermal loads remains moderately uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of bond coats using the HVAF-i7 torch with identical FeCoNiCrAl 15–45 μm powders and substrate conditions. The control group will be deposited with the current spray distance, while the experimental group will use the reduced spray distance (300–350 mm). All other deposition parameters should be maintained constant. After deposition, perform comparative analyses.
measurements: Oxidation levels (using surface analysis such as XPS or EDS)
Durability under simulated high-temperature thermal-barrier service
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coatings produced at the reduced spray distance do not show a statistically significant increase in thickness and deposition efficiency compared to the control or if the improved thickness coincides with unacceptable oxidation or adhesion degradation, then the hypothesis will be falsified.

Thus, in-flight oxidation of the AlCoCrFeNi particle during the spraying process can be beneficial for the tribological performance of the HEA coatings. Due to high specific surface area, the powder can oxidize differently from the cast bulk alloy. Moreover, the formation of multiple oxides—alumina, chromia, and spinel—changes the residual particle’s core composition and can lead to phase destabilization. Therefore, understanding the regularity of the oxidation behavior and phase transformation of the high-entropy powder at different conditions should be necessary for the production of a coating with high and determined property levels. In this work, the oxidation behavior and phase transformations of FeNiCoCrMo0.5Al1.3 high-entropy alloy powder, produced via gas atomization, were studied. Powder oxidation and phase transformations were studied under HVOF deposition, during continuous heating, and under prolonged isothermal annealing at 800 °C. FeNiCoCrMo0.5Al1.3 HVOF coatings were produced using various distances from the spray nozzle to the substrate to produce coatings with different oxide contents, and the coatings’ properties were investigated.

cited_evidence.text: The power loaded on the target and the substrate temperature determine the energy of sputtered atoms and deposited atoms, respectively. Besides, the crystal orientation of substrate would affect the island formation during the film deposition. Therefore, the power, substrate temperature and the type of substrate are three important parameters that could affect the phase and microstructure of HEF. FeCoNiCrAl HEFs with different deposition conditions were prepared (summarized in the Table 1) to investigate the effects of the parameters. Figure 2 is the SEM images of HEF samples with different deposition parameters, including plan-view images (Figure 2(a1–f1)) and corresponding cross-sectional images (Figure 2(a2–f2)). All of the images have the same scale bar, as marked in Figure 2(a2). Figure 2a–c represent the images of the HEF samples deposited on substrate of Si (100) with the power of 300 W. The substrate temperatures (T) are room temperature (RT), 250 °C and 350 °C respectively. The surface of these samples is intact without holes or cracks, and the thickness of the films is about 975 ± 5 nm.

drafts.hypothesis: Increasing the nozzle-to-substrate distance during HVAF-i7 spraying will elevate particle velocity, which in turn improves the deposition efficiency and enables the formation of thicker, adherent FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy bond coats with minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
drafts.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy powder with a 15–45 μm particle size used in HVAF deposition.
drafts.intervention: Adjust the spray distance to 300–350 mm on the HVAF-i7 torch.
drafts.conditions: HVAF-i7 deposition under standard gas flow and feed rate settings, applied on substrates including those with internal diameters as small as 120 mm, with all other process parameters held constant.
drafts.structural_mediator: Enhanced particle impact energy due to increased particle velocity, resulting in better particle deformation and bonding upon impact.
drafts.mechanism: By increasing the spray distance, the particles gain higher velocity and consequently greater kinetic energy before impacting the substrate. This leads to improved flattening and inter-particle bonding, which enhances deposition efficiency, leading to thicker coatings while maintaining low oxidation levels.
drafts.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline condition (using the default spray distance with 15–45 μm feedstock), the adjusted spray distance will yield a significantly thicker and more adherent bond coat with minimal in-flight oxidation.
drafts.baseline: Coatings produced using the HVAF-i7 torch with 15–45 μm feedstock at the default spray distance, which result in acceptable quality yet insufficient thickness.
drafts.boundary: This intervention is expected to remain effective under typical HVAF-i7 operational settings and for the FeCoNiCrAl alloy formulation. Its effectiveness may vary if the feedstock size distribution or gas composition is significantly altered.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform a controlled experiment using the HVAF-i7 torch with identical batches of FeCoNiCrAl 15–45 μm powder. Use two spray conditions: one with the default spray distance and one with the adjusted distance of 300–350 mm. Ensure that all other process parameters (e.g., gas flow, feed rate, substrate type) are held constant. Assess the resulting bond coats for thickness, adhesion strength, oxidation level, and high-temperature durability.
measurements: Adhesion strength (e.g., via standardized pull-off tests)
Oxidation content (e.g., using XPS or SEM-EDS analysis)
Durability under simulated high-temperature thermal-barrier service conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis will be falsified if the bond coats produced at the increased spray distance do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement in thickness and do not meet or exceed the adhesion, oxidation, and durability benchmarks established by the baseline condition.

drafts.hypothesis: Increasing the particle velocity during HVAF-i7 deposition by reducing the spray distance (and/or optimizing nozzle design) to the 300–350 mm range will overcome the current thickness limitation for FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy bond coats.
drafts.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy powders with a feedstock size of 15–45 μm prepared for HVAF deposition.
drafts.intervention: Adjust the HVAF-i7 torch parameters to increase the particle velocity by reducing the spray distance to approximately 300–350 mm (or applying an equivalent nozzle design modification that boosts particle acceleration).
drafts.conditions: Deposition using an HVAF-i7 system under conditions suitable for internal diameters as small as 120 mm and expected high-temperature thermal-barrier service; similar process duration and environmental control as in the prior studies.
drafts.structural_mediator: Enhanced impact energy of the particles, leading to improved splat formation and inter-particle bonding which contributes to increased deposition efficiency.
drafts.mechanism: Higher particle velocity increases the kinetic energy of the feedstock particles. When these high-energy particles impact the substrate, they flatten more effectively and adhere better, thereby building up thicker coatings while maintaining quality with minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
drafts.predicted_outcome: An increase in the overall bond coat thickness compared to the baseline produced with conventional spray distances, with the coating retaining its required adhesion, low oxidation levels, and durability during high-temperature service.
drafts.baseline: Coatings produced with a 15–45 μm feedstock via HVAF-i7 at the previously used spray distance, which, although of acceptable quality, exhibit inadequate thickness.
drafts.boundary: This intervention is expected to be effective when the spray distance is reduced to the specified 300–350 mm range and the process parameters are controlled to avoid detrimental effects such as excessive thermal load or oxidation. Its effectiveness may be limited if particle velocities become too high, potentially compromising coating adhesion or oxidation resistance.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a controlled experiment comparing two sets of HVAF-i7 depositions using FeCoNiCrAl powders (15–45 μm) on substrates with 120 mm internal diameters. One set (control) will use the conventional spray distance that has previously yielded acceptable quality but insufficient thickness, while the experimental set will use a reduced spray distance (300–350 mm) and/or an optimized nozzle design intended to enhance particle velocity. All other process parameters are maintained constant.
measurements: Thermal stability after simulated high-temperature service
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the experimental set does not show a statistically significant increase in coating thickness and deposition efficiency, relative to the control, or if the coating quality (oxidation levels, adhesion, thermal stability) is compromised, then the hypothesis would be falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: Increasing the particle velocity during HVAF-i7 deposition—by adjusting torch parameters to achieve a spray distance of approximately 300–350 mm—will boost the kinetic energy of the 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock particles, resulting in a thicker, well-adhered bond coat with minimal as-sprayed oxidation compared to the current HVAF-i7 process.
drafts.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy feedstock with particle sizes between 15 and 45 μm, as used in prior HVAF-M3 coatings.
drafts.intervention: Adjust the HVAF-i7 torch operating conditions to increase particle velocity (e.g., by modifying fuel gas flow and related parameters) and set the spray distance to around 300–350 mm.
drafts.conditions: Deposition performed using the HVAF-i7 torch in an environment suitable for high-velocity oxygen-fuel spraying; target applications include internal diameters down to 120 mm and high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
drafts.structural_mediator: Enhanced in-flight particle momentum leading to improved particle splat formation and interlamellar bonding at impact.
drafts.mechanism: Higher particle velocity increases the kinetic energy of the powder particles upon impact, promoting a denser, thicker coating with stronger adhesion while reducing the dwell-time at critical oxidation temperatures, thereby limiting excessive oxidation and ensuring coating integrity.
drafts.predicted_outcome: The intervention should yield a bond coat that is significantly thicker than that achieved with the unmodified HVAF-i7 process while maintaining acceptable adhesion and low as-sprayed oxidation, thereby matching or surpassing the baseline performance of HVAF-M3 coatings.
drafts.baseline: Coatings produced with 15–45 μm feedstock using the HVAF-M3 torch, which have acceptable quality but with different deposition dynamics compared to HVAF-i7.
drafts.boundary: The approach is effective only if the increased particle velocity does not induce overheating, excess oxidation, or other deleterious microstructural changes; the optimized spray distance and torch settings must be maintained within the operational limits of the HVAF-i7 system, particularly when spraying within confined internal diameters.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of FeCoNiCrAl bond coats on substrate samples using the HVAF-i7 system: one set with standard parameters and one with increased particle velocity and a spray distance of 300–350 mm. Ensure identical feedstock and substrate conditions. Assess the resulting coatings for thickness, adhesion, oxidation level (via microscopy and surface analysis), and mechanical performance.
measurements: Coating thickness using cross-sectional optical or electron microscopy
Oxidation level via EDS or X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the modified deposition parameters do not yield a statistically significant increase in coating thickness (or if they result in unacceptable levels of oxidation or decreased adhesion compared to the baseline), then the hypothesis that increasing particle velocity overcomes the thickness limitation is falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: Reducing the nozzle-to-substrate distance to achieve higher particle velocities in the HVAF-i7 process will overcome the thickness limitation while maintaining low oxidation and good adhesion for FeCoNiCrAl bond coats.
drafts.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy powder with a feedstock size of 15–45 μm, as currently used in HVAF-i7 deposition yielding acceptable coating quality but inadequate thickness.
drafts.intervention: Adjust the spray parameters by reducing the nozzle-to-substrate distance (targeting near 300 mm) on the HVAF-i7 torch to increase particle velocity during deposition.
drafts.conditions: Deposition using the HVAF-i7 torch under conditions similar to those for MCrAlY conventional bond coats, especially in applications requiring internal diameters as small as 120 mm and high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
drafts.structural_mediator: Increased particle kinetic energy during flight improves deposition efficiency and reduces in-flight residence time, thereby limiting undesired oxidation while promoting better inter-particle bonding.
drafts.mechanism: The reduced spray distance leads to a higher incoming velocity of the particles. This enhancement increases the impact energy on the substrate, resulting in a thicker, more adherent coating with minimal oxidation as the particles have less time to oxidize in flight.
drafts.predicted_outcome: An improvement in coating thickness relative to the current HVAF-i7 baseline, while retaining coating integrity and low as-sprayed oxidation levels. The increased thickness should not compromise the mechanical or thermal protection properties required for high-temperature service.
drafts.baseline: Using 15–45 μm feedstock with the current HVAF-i7 parameters (non-optimized spray distance) that produce acceptable coating quality but an inadequate thickness compared to HVAF-M3 outcomes.
drafts.boundary: This intervention is expected to be effective when applied under similar ambient conditions and with feedstock parameters consistent with those used in prior conventional MCrAlY bond coat studies, particularly for applications involving small internal diameters (~120 mm) and thermal-barrier environments.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct two series of HVAF-i7 depositions using FeCoNiCrAl 15–45 μm feedstock: one at the current standard nozzle-to-substrate distance and one reduced to approximately 300 mm. All other parameters should be held constant. Compare the coating thickness, microstructure (via SEM/XRD), oxidation levels (via EDS or XPS), and adhesion tests.
measurements: Oxide content and phase composition (using XRD and EDS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If reducing the spray distance to 300 mm does not result in a statistically significant increase in coating thickness or if it leads to unacceptable changes in oxidation levels or adhesion compared to the baseline HVAF-i7 deposition, the hypothesis will be falsified.
